# Grid sparkline cells stay blank in a popup for rows recycled after the pane moved there

## Context

The operator, 2026-10-11 02:0xZ, watching the film take at PR #19587's head live on the stage display: "offscreen canvases do not show inside the grid inside the popup." Confirmed on the recording (take `2026-10-11T02-05-48-526Z`, the matrix window's frames at 90.5–97.5 s): after the Workstation's 100k-row matrix (`Workstation.view.ScalePane`, `type: 'sparkline'` column — the framework's OffscreenCanvas path) is torn out into its own window (`?popout=scale`) and that window is grown, the rows that were mounted at the move paint their sparklines; after the jump to row 50000 and the drag-scroll throw, every recycled row shows an empty Living signal column while the other columns (text, progress bars, the component column's buttons) render. The same grid in the main window paints its sparklines on scroll (take `2026-10-11T00-55-16-516Z`, the strokes at 90–95 s).

Observation, separated from inference: observed = blank sparkline cells for rows that enter the viewport after the move; the rows present at the move paint. Inferred (unverified) = the incremental cell path (row recycling → the sparkline cell's canvas registration / repaint with the Canvas worker) resolves the window or the canvas handle of the pane's former window, while the full re-mount at the move registers the visible cells in the popup's document correctly.

## The Problem

A torn-out grid is a first-class Workstation state (the dock's vessels), and the sparkline column is the grid's OffscreenCanvas showcase. In a vessel the column goes blank the moment the user scrolls — a visible defect in the product's most demonstrative pane, and the film's close (#19584) cannot be shot until it paints.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/grid/column/Sparkline.mjs` (the column), `src/component/Sparkline.mjs` (the cell component) and `src/canvas/Sparkline.mjs` (the Canvas-worker side) own the path; `Neo.grid.Body` recycles row/cell instances on scroll (`createRowPool`, the column pool). The pane keeps its instance across the tear-out (the dock's claim, proven by the film's identity checks); its DOM is re-created in the popup's document.
- The tear-out and the popup are the dock's (`src/dashboard/dock/*`, `VesselWorkspace`); the film's `vessel-resize` grow (PR #19587) only moves and resizes the frame through the owner-granted routes — the blank cells follow the scroll, not the resize (the rows mounted before the jump kept their paint through the grow).

## The Fix

Owner's investigation, with a falsifier first: a whitebox e2e that tears the scale pane out (the existing `tear-out` executor or the dock API), scrolls the grid in the vessel, and asserts per recycled sparkline cell that the Canvas worker received its registration and paint for the popup's window (or that the cell's canvas has a non-blank bitmap via the popup page). Then fix where the incremental path binds the window / canvas handle. Not a film change.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A whitebox e2e reproduces the blank recycled cells in a vessel at the current head and passes after the fix: after a scroll in the torn-out matrix, every visible sparkline cell paints (Canvas-worker receipt or a non-blank bitmap in the popup page).
- [ ] The main-window path is unchanged (the existing film witness's `canvas-update` cue and the dense tour stay green).
- [ ] Post-merge, deferred to #15252: a film take at a head containing this fix shows the Living signal column painted through the midpoint jump and the throw in the matrix window.

## Out of Scope

- The film's choreography (#19584 / PR #19587) and the vessel's road home (two defect-notes, 2026-10-11).
- #19585 (the SharedCanvas pointer origin after resize): a different canvas symptom.

### @neo-gpt-emmy - 2026-10-11T02:41:14Z

Reproduced and isolated in headless Chrome using merged Engine `5b958c314967730ff5102df5a592ad598da2f36c` plus the five film modules from `39875770e0ce33737c0184d20db293a6edf616b1` (served at the HTTP boundary so SharedWorker imports consume the exact candidate).

The complete 34-beat film ran through tear-out, vessel resize, midpoint and throw. All 9 visible popup Sparkline canvases were blank (`countPixelsUnlikeDominant.unlike = 0`), while text and other cell content remained present. Their component state was mounted, correctly bound to the popup, and populated with 12 values, but `offscreenRegistered` was false.

A second run traced the cause: the normal unmount → window change → remount sequence occurred. In the popup, all 27 `transferControlToOffscreen()` calls succeeded, but **the window had no Canvas Worker connection and all 27 `Manager.sendMessage('canvas', …)` calls returned null**. No registration acknowledgement could arrive. This falsifies a missing-remount explanation; the constructor-only worker bootstrap had not run again for the retained instances.

The minimal candidate ensures this window's existing Canvas Worker through `Manager.startWorker({name: 'canvas'})` before `DomAccess.transferCanvasToWorker` extracts the canvas. Replaying the same full film now gives 8/8 visible registered and painted canvases (373 pixels unlike background on the clipped cell; 2,036–2,478 on full cells), with no browser errors. Permanent cold-transport and recycled-popup regression coverage is in progress. The native take remains a separate post-merge acceptance step on #15252; this is not a native-media acceptance claim.
